links.comparator_used: Basic AI-CDSS showing the sella outline without model explanation, previous publications or confidence labels (the Enhanced arm bundled these with the confidence labels)
links.outcome: Self-reported clinician trust (1-7) when AI performed worst, as a measure of trust calibration; also user DICE performance and its dispersion
links.effect: Worst AI clip: median trust 3.00 Enhanced vs 3.67 Basic (U=668, p=.035). Final clip: 3.67 vs 4.33 (U=687, p=.019). Best AI clip: median trust 5.00 in both arms (p=.521). Performance did not differ significantly between groups on the best or worst AI clips. Senior clinicians on the best AI clip: 0.95 vs 0.90 (p=.066). Dispersion when AI was inaccurate: IQR 0.07 vs 0.21 (p=.004).
links.quote: However, when AI performed worst, trust was significantly lower for the Enhanced group (3.00 vs 3.67, U=668, p=.035), sustained in the final clip (3.67 vs 4.33 U=687, p=.019).

design_hint: Model explanation and confidence labels in AI decision support interface
